title: Epoch AI finds AI acknowledgments in math papers jumped to 25% in four months
key_facts: Epoch AI published an analysis of arXiv math preprints on 18 Sep 2026.
The share of papers acknowledging AI use rose from 4% in April 2026 to 25% in August 2026.
More than half of papers in three math subfields acknowledge AI; differential geometry rose from about 8% to 57%.
6% of August preprints credited AI with a substantive contribution, which Epoch compares to a co-author's role.
Epoch filtered papers by AI-related keywords, then used GPT-5.6 Sol to categorise contributions, with Claude Fable 5 validating; human reviewers agreed with the classifications 93% of the time.
Established authors who published regularly before 2023 disclose AI help at similar rates.
Epoch released its data publicly under a Creative Commons BY licence; the figures track disclosure, not total AI use.
quote_evidence: It found that the share of papers acknowledging AI use rose from 4% in April 2026 to 25% by August 2026.
According to Epoch, 6% of the August preprints credited AI with a substantive contribution to the research.
The acknowledgment data alone tracks disclosure, and disclosure is what researchers choose to put in writing.
why_it_matters_hint: Disclosure norms are moving faster than the rules for crediting AI contributions.
event_date: Epoch AI analysis published 18 Sep 2026 (data April to August 2026)
notes: Older analysis re-reported by Crypto Briefing on 9 Oct 2026; scored down as stale. Epoch's own page not read.
